Lab — unlisted and noindexed. The live chart at tracking-london-crime is untouched: this page carries its own inlined copies of the engines, so nothing on the site changes until the sprint is published. What is new here is the compact layout for narrow and short screens. Built 01 Sep 2026 12:14.

Picker experiment — does your phone make you press “Done”?

On a desktop a <select> drops open and one click both chooses and closes it. Some Android browsers — Samsung Internet in particular — open a bottom sheet instead and want a second press to confirm. That is the browser's decision, not the page's, but two things about the control might tip it one way or the other: whether the list is grouped, and how long it is. These three are identical to the chart's own crime picker except in those two respects. Open each and note whether choosing an item closes it by itself.

If all three behave the same, it is simply what that browser does with a <select>, and the only way round it would be a hand-built menu — which costs the OS scrolling, the free truncation and the accessibility that made native the right call. Worth knowing either way. It is also worth opening the page in Chrome on the same phone: if Chrome behaves and Samsung Internet does not, that settles it.
